title: one-step equations with an unknown number, using all operations

lesson.title: Finding the Missing Number

steps.say: Hi friend, it's Ms. Yuanyuan! Yesterday I went to the corner store in Victoria with eleven dollars in my pocket. My grandma handed me four more dollars, and then I had fifteen dollars altogether. But imagine I forgot how much I started with. I would only know this: something, plus four, makes fifteen. That mystery something is what today's lesson is all about.

Here is the big secret. An equals sign is really a balance scale, like the ones we use in science class. Whatever sits on the left side must weigh exactly the same as whatever sits on the right side. Our mystery box plus four dollars on the left balances perfectly with fifteen dollars on the right. Nothing tips over.

visual.caption: The two sides weigh the same

steps.say: So how do we catch the mystery number? We do the opposite. Four dollars were added on, so to find what was there before, we take those four dollars back off. Fifteen take away four is eleven. Let's check it: eleven plus four really is fifteen. It balances, so eleven is right!

visual.caption: The whole is 15, so the missing part is 11

steps.say: Now let's try one where the mystery is in the middle. My cousin Jonah has twelve dollars saved and he wants twenty dollars for a movie ticket and popcorn. Twelve plus how many more makes twenty? Watch the number line. We hop from twelve up to twenty, and that hop is eight. Twelve plus eight is twenty. Perfect!

visual.caption: Jumping from 12 to 20 is a jump of 8

steps.say: Here comes a trickier one, with subtracting. I had fifteen stickers, I gave some away, and eleven were left. How many did I give away? Fifteen take away the mystery equals eleven. Think of it as the difference between fifteen and eleven. Fifteen minus eleven is four, so I gave away four stickers. Check it: fifteen take away four leaves eleven. It works!

The same trick works for times and sharing too. Three friends each grabbed the same number of blueberries from a BC berry farm, and together they took eighteen. Three times what equals eighteen? Multiplying is the opposite of dividing, so we divide: eighteen shared into three equal groups is six each. Look, three groups of six dots really does make eighteen.

So here's the whole method in one breath. Adding is undone by subtracting, subtracting is undone by adding, times is undone by dividing, and dividing is undone by times. Do the opposite move to the number you know, and the mystery pops right out. Then always pop your answer back into the equation to make sure both sides still balance.
You did it! Every one of these puzzles is just a balance scale asking you a polite question, and you already know how to answer it. Give the practice one a try — I know you've got this.

lesson.answer: To find a missing number, do the opposite operation — then check that both sides balance.

practice.question: Liam is saving for a hockey puck set that costs 20 dollars. He already has 13 dollars. Using the equation 13 + n = 20, how many more dollars does Liam need?
practice.answer: n = 7. Because 20 − 13 = 7, and checking it, 13 + 7 = 20. Liam needs 7 more dollars.
